mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the unemployment rate increase does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decrease does not correlate with subsequent consumer sentiment or retail sales indicators.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent manufacturing and production indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the CPIAUCSL YoY is above 2%, the combination signals an accommodative monetary policy despite inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent market performance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent employment and wage growth indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% YoY and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.5% YoY, the combination signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 10% YoY and UNRATE decreases > 0.5% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of housing starts and unemployment rate changes does not correlate with subsequent economic growth indicators.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a quarter, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS increase does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.
